comment: Grammar injection: re-applies the MFront rules with injectionSelector 'L:source.mfront -comment -string', so they also match inside scopes nested by the embedded source.cpp grammar. The base grammar's rules only live at the root level, so once such a nested scope opens, every following '@Xxx' keyword would lose keyword.control.mfront for the rest of the file. The 'L:' prefix makes the injection apply on the left, i.e. before the grammar's own patterns, which is what lets it reach into those nested scopes - and is also why '#description-block' has to be repeated here: without it the injected '#keywords' would match '@Description' first and the block body would fall through to source.cpp. '-comment -string' excludes commented-out and quoted text, so a keyword inside '// @UseQt true;' is not re-highlighted as live code. The rules are NOT duplicated: they are included by reference from source.mfront's repository, so the keyword list has a single definition.
